title: Constitution of India
source: curated summary - authentic text at the India Code URL

sections.heading: Equality before law
sections.text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

sections.heading: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech etc.
sections.text: Guarantees to citizens freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession, each subject to reasonable restrictions on the grounds specified in the Article.

sections.heading: Protection in respect of conviction for offences
sections.text: No ex post facto criminal liability, no double jeopardy, and no compulsion to be a witness against oneself.

sections.heading: Protection of life and personal liberty
sections.text: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law - read to require that the procedure be fair, just and reasonable.

sections.heading: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
sections.text: Grounds of arrest to be communicated, right to consult a legal practitioner, and production before a magistrate within 24 hours.

sections.heading: Remedies for enforcement of fundamental rights
sections.text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of fundamental rights. Itself a fundamental right.

sections.heading: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
sections.text: Every High Court may issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and for any other purpose, throughout its territorial jurisdiction. Wider than Article 32.

sections.heading: Power of superintendence over all courts by the High Court
sections.text: Supervisory jurisdiction over all courts and tribunals within the High Court's territories.

sections.heading: Persons not to be deprived of property save by authority of law
sections.text: No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. A constitutional right, not a fundamental right.
